source.title: Language Mapping of Schools in Jharkhand: Phase I — Survey Report
institutional_context: Jharkhand Council of Educational Research and Training
source.verification_level: direct report PDF with table/page locators plus LLF report index corroboration

exact_locators.supported_metadata_or_scope: The report states that phase I covered 8,244 schools across 7 Jharkhand districts and focused on language-of-home/language-of-instruction conditions in government schools.

exact_locators.locator: PDF/report section 3.4, Limitations of the Study
exact_locators.supported_metadata_or_scope: Teacher-filled survey responses and teacher-perceived proficiency measures are explicitly identified as limitations; the survey did not collect broader community sociolinguistic insights.
exact_locators.promotion_boundary: limitations are retained alongside every numeric locator; figures are not treated as direct language proficiency tests or community-validated cultural facts

exact_locators.locator: PDF p.19, Table 1 — Top 10 Languages with the Most Number of Speakers Amongst Grade 1 Students in the surveyed districts of Jharkhand
exact_locators.supported_metadata_or_scope: Mundari is listed at 7.32% among Grade 1 students in the seven surveyed districts.
exact_locators.promotion_boundary: aggregate survey statistic only; not a Census population estimate and not generalized beyond the survey frame

exact_locators.locator: PDF p.24, Table 2 — District-wise Teachers' Proficiency in Students' Home Languages
exact_locators.supported_metadata_or_scope: For Khunti, Mundari is the most common listed home language; the table reports 393 schools, 145 teachers reporting minimal proficiency and 366 reporting functional proficiency in speaking that home language.
exact_locators.promotion_boundary: self-reported/teacher-reported survey statistic with the report's stated limitations; no individual-level or cultural inference

exact_locators.locator: PDF p.31, Table 4 — Prominent Link languages spoken in the Survey Districts
exact_locators.supported_metadata_or_scope: Mundari is included among the prominent link languages listed for the surveyed districts.
exact_locators.promotion_boundary: report-defined survey output only; no claim of universal link-language status across Jharkhand

deduplication.repository_search: No prior run261/LLF Jharkhand Phase-I exact-locator audit was found in the mlhkp-v2 source-census tree before creation.
deduplication.canonicalization_action: treat the LLF report index page, direct PDF and UNESCO later citation as representations/corroboration of one survey/report family, not separate MLHKP identities
deduplication.reason_count_neutral: The 73 unresolved WEB-MUN leads have not been fully reconciled against this report family; no controlled identity total is incremented until deterministic reconciliation closes.

rights_access_consent_cultural_boundary.notes: Public PDF access supports exact citation/verification, not blanket redistribution or model-training permission. Only aggregate survey-level Mundari locators are recorded; no names, raw respondent records, cultural narratives or sensitive community content are ingested.

cross_checks.source: Language and Learning Foundation — Multilingual Education page
cross_checks.observation: LLF publicly indexes 'LM Report Jharkhand Phase 1' among its State Reports.

cross_checks.source: UNESCO State of the Education Report 2025, Case Study 16 (published 2026)
cross_checks.observation: UNESCO describes the Jharkhand Palash programme and cites the 2024 language mapping survey across 8,244 primary schools in seven districts, including Mundari among home languages.
cross_checks.role: independent later corroboration of survey/program context; not substituted for the report's exact tables

blocked_attempts.observation: A page-image screenshot request for the direct LLF PDF intermittently returned an internal fetch error after the PDF text layer had been successfully retrieved.
blocked_attempts.disposition: retain exact text-layer page/table locator, explicitly log screenshot failure, and do not claim image-level verification
